options: Hff... brr...
It's cold...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Are you still cold, Doctor? I should've reminded you to bring heavier clothes.
Amiya clutches your fingertips. Her palm is cold too.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Hang in there for a while. Things will be better in Tsarevgrad.

options: I thought this would be another solo audience.
I thought the Tsar would be more wary of us.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: On the contrary, His Imperial Majesty was very impressed by Rhodes Island's feats in the Far North. He is eager to see you.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Especially after hearing that the leader of Rhodes Island is so young.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I didn't do very much...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Now is not the time for humility. Make the most of the good first impression—it can only be a good thing for the meeting.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: There are a few things about Grypherburg that I must communicate before we meet His Imperial Majesty.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: First... I'm sure you're not oblivious as to why the Tsar has chosen to grant you an audience.

options: While His Majesty is known for his benevolence—
He would not give us access to the Sarcophagus for no reason.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You want the secrets of the Sarcophagus. So do we.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: We hope that this meeting will result in mutually beneficial cooperation.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You understand the most pressing matter facing Ursus...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Or at the very least, Grypherburg.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: It has been two months since the Fourth Army began pressing toward Grypherburg. Now they remain in a tense standoff against the Second Army along the eastern shore of Lake Neva, with the occasional skirmish.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: They have not gone any further for now, but we can ill-afford to be optimistic.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: They continue to petition the State Council, demanding full support for the war that they intend to start.

options: Most curious.
If the Fourth Army's intention is to start a war of conquest—
They should be on the borders of Ursus, not the outskirts of Grypherburg.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Hah... everyone knows what these traitors are planning. They continue their despicable attacks on the Council.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: There was an attempt on Chairman Witte's life the day after the Fourth Army's First Division was routed. The assassin's methods bore clear associations with those of the Fourth Army.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Yet in the face of such provocation, the Royal Guard somehow failed to capture or kill the assassin.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: There is also reason to believe that the assassin's accomplice, or accomplices, remain at large in the city.

options: The Fourth Army is only the most immediate issue.
At the end of the day, Ursus must confront the reality of ore exhaustion.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Exactly. Most see two paths before the empire, war or peace, yet neither is sufficiently convincing to everyone.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: His Imperial Majesty places his hopes in the Sarcophagus, currently under the First Army's control.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: A breakthrough in this direction may represent the empire's last hope for a solution, absurd as it may sound.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Even so...

options: Research into the Sarcophagus is not going smoothly.
The Council faces issues beyond research progress.
We were not invited as scholars.
We're here at the invitation of the Council, not the First Army.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Astute as always, Dr. {@nickname}.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: However, I would recommend against such overt astuteness during your audience with the Tsar.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: It appears that the First Army is indeed hiding something... though it's better for you to hear from His Imperial Majesty himself.

options: What do you think of the Tsar?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Even in a private setting like this, such a question is bound to raise suspicions.

options: I just want to hear your thoughts.
I just want to be prepared.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You must have heard rumors about him from various channels. It's not my place to try to change opinions. All I can do is answer truthfully.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: If there is anyone in Ursus who will fight to the bitter end for her, it is His Imperial Majesty.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: For he has nothing, save Ursus.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: ...Off-limits...

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: This place is off-limits! Go away!

steps.name: Worried Citizen
steps.text: Please, sir, I'm not Infected! The new pass—see here, the pass! We bought it, we're law-abiding citizens...

steps.name: Worried Citizen
steps.text: We must deliver these goods in time! The nobles won't take them otherwise, even if they're unspoiled, and we'll be ruined!

steps.name: Lamenting Citizen
steps.text: We can't afford heat anymore, and our child is sick in bed... please, have mercy and let us pass—

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: Tsarevgrad Raion is currently under lockdown. Not even a pass made of gold will buy you passage.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: Take your things and leave. An announcement will be made once the lockdown is lifted.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Is that a roadblock?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Stay in the vehicle. I'll check it out.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: Didn't you hear me? This place is off-limits—

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Zdravstvuyte.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: (Salutes)

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: What do you need, ma'am?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: His Imperial Majesty wishes to meet these good people.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: Tsarevgrad Raion is on lockdown. Even deliveries of necessities must be met by someone from inside.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: By order of the Tsar.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You're doing your duty, I understand.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: But I'm curious, what do you do when His Imperial Majesty's orders contradict themselves?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Because I'm operating by order of the Tsar myself. In fact, I have his edict right here.
The young Imperial Guard unrolls a piece of paper with a bright red seal on the bottom corner.
It is the Tsar's administrative seal.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I understand. We can wait a little while, if there is some difficulty.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: I'm afraid waiting won't do any good, ma'am. The situation is unlikely to change until the culprit is caught.
Eloysius fights her urge to roll her eyes. She puts the edict back, places her hand on her sword hilt, and straightens her back.
She looks up again, her expression completely changed.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: The Grypherburg Police are under the jurisdiction of the Ursus Guard. You have people inside Tsarevgrad.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: All you need to do is inform your commander that His Imperial Majesty's guests have arrived. The rest is no longer your concern.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: But—

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: 'Lieutenant Eloysius Vasilyevna Gorchekova, Imperial Guard Tsar's Battalion, accepts all responsibility for carrying out His Imperial Majesty's orders and consents to all inspections.'

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Pass that message to your commander.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Can you remember the whole thing?

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: ...Yes, ma'am.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: Please wait here for a moment.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: One more thing.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: The couple hauling the goods over there, they are with us too.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: The items are meant for the Tsar. You may include them in your report.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Done.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The road's not open?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: It's open, but only for us.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Let's not waste the opportunity.

steps.name: Voice from Inside
steps.text: Enter.

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: Please wait here with the guests, Lieutenant Gorchekova.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Thank you.
You look around as the servant departs.
The room's furnishing is minimalistic compared to the luxury that you saw on your way here, but its owner's position of authority is obvious.
The curtains are closed even during the day, electric lights shine brightly, documents are stacked up on a cart, and the corners of the table have been repaired with gold.

options: The office seems to be in frequent use.
You brought us in here directly?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: How can you tell?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: There are multiple rooms with identical furnishings in the Amber Palace, as a safety measure. This is just one of them.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You should not make blind guesses.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: What else did you think we need?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: These may be unusual times, but nothing opens doors like one's rank in Tsarevgrad, even without all the medals on my chest.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: The only people allowed to access this area are the Tsar, his most trusted ministers, and people who have been granted special permission.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You should therefore be respectful. Conversation is permitted, but I would refrain from commentary, if I were you.

options: I meant no offense.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Just keep your patience, as you did last time, until His Imperial Majesty is finished...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: with the things that are troubling him right now.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: —Chairman?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I thought Your High Excellency was still recovering at home—

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I'm here on His Imperial Majesty's behalf. He has urgent matters to attend to.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Your work here is done, lieutenant. I would meet with our guests privately.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I've spoken to your father. He is concerned about how busy you have been lately, and hopes that you come home once in a while, if you could.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Your High Excellency's concern is appreciated, Chairman Witte.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I will take my leave.
The young woman claps her heels together in a military salute, then turns and departs.
The chairman watches her leave, only turning around once the door is fully closed.

options: Greetings, Chairman Witte.
Your reputation precedes you, Chairman Witte.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Greetings, guests from afar. Thank you for accepting our invitation.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I see we have learned of each other, in different ways.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Please, take a seat.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: There is little time for pleasantries. Let us be frank and honest with each other.

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: Your Imperial Majesty, it is my honor to report the progress that the First Army has made on Project Zero.

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: Her High Excellency the Marshal understands that you are much troubled by matters of state and the traitors' movements. I hope the news I bring will do something to soothe these troubles.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: ...Where is Marshal Buterina?

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: She remains in her domain.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: She's supervising Project Zero, and she should be the one reporting to me.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Why are you here in her stead?

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: I apologize, Your Imperial Majesty, I should have explained.

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: The Marshal's son, Anatoliy, was attacked a few days ago, and remains in serious condition. Her High Excellency has no choice but to remain behind, both to punish the perpetrators, and to prevent further instability.

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: After all, we are not like the Fourth Army; no hint of rebellion is permitted, whether internal or external.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Why have I not been informed?

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: It is the Marshal's private family matter, after all.

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: Now, if you have no other questions, I will continue my report.

steps.name: Angry Servant
steps.text: How could you speak to the Tsar like this? You insolent—

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: I am simply stating the facts, yet you make a serious accusation. I am fully able to take responsibility for my words. Can you say the same?

steps.name: Angry Servant
steps.text: Why you—!

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: That will do... continue, Kapitan.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Grypherburg has already committed tremendous resources to Project Zero. If there is no material progress...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: There will be consequences.

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: Rest assured, you will not be disappointed.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Before we begin, allow me to satisfy my curiosity.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I understand Rhodes Island came a long way to the Far North, rescuing the Infected miners there.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: May I ask why?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Rhodes Island is a medical concern, and our mission is to combat Oripathy. We are committed to providing treatment for any Oripathy sufferer who needs it.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Does the Empire of Ursus feel the need to question every act of kindness towards the Infected?
You tug the corner of Amiya's skirt.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: ...Infected, Cautus, leader of Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: You are known by the mononym Amiya, correct?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Understand that I am not seeking to interrogate Rhodes Island on your aims.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Lieutenant Gorchekova thinks highly of you. She is a good soldier, and I trust that her assessment is a result of objective observation.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Let me make it clear that I am very grateful to you for your actions in the Far North, which laid the foundation for this meeting.

options: We mean no offense, Your Excellency.
Allow me to introduce myself.
I am Dr. {@nickname}.
I'm Rhodes Island's medical advisor.
I'm Rhodes Island's expert on Originium.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Medical advisor?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I take it there is more to this title than meets the eye, if you're here as a representative of Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: An Originium expert. Your arrival may be serendipitous for us.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Go ahead, Doctor.

options: We know Ursus is looking for Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: 'Kal'tsit'...

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Indeed, perhaps we should dispense with the formalities.
You notice that Witte tapped the floor with his walking stick gently, discreetly shifting his center of gravity.
He is considering what to say.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: If not for the deep-rooted corruption within the Third Bureau, this name would have been known to our secret police sooner, not recently discovered in old piles of paper.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: This is a good starting point, and you've brought it up of your own accord without trying to hide it. Perhaps we can come to an agreement.

options: Are you looking for Kal'tsit in order to open the Sarcophagus?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Obviously, as Elotta has told you.
He takes a meaningful pause and glances at you.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Due to various circumstances, we have had to... restructure our energy planning. It is the source of the empire's present dilemma.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Research into the Sarcophagus has resumed, but things are not going well.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: We need Kal'tsit and her knowledge from Chernobog to help the people survive this winter.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: By studying the Sarcophagus as she did in the Chernobog lab?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I see you understand that it is the fastest way.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Now, can you tell me where Kal'tsit is?

options: Why do you ask?
You don't believe what the lieutenant told you.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Please understand that I ask out of an abundance of caution.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: After all, we both know that Kal'tsit was 'alive and kicking', so to speak, for all those years that the secret police thought she was dead.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I hope our conversation will not stand on unnecessary deception.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I ask not because I don't trust Elotta, but because I need to make sure that Rhodes Island is in a position to assist our research into the Sarcophagus.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: We all keep certain secrets, of course, but some questions must be confronted, not evaded.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit is... indisposed.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: And if I may be frank, we also have reservations about this cooperation.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We want to know if Ursus's ongoing research into the Sarcophagus will lead to a repeat of the Chernobog tragedy.

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: ...That concludes the report. In summary, the First Army is currently holding position in the southwest.

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: Several shells powered by Project Zero energy were tested several days ago at a location in the wilderness of the Central Governorate.

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: The destruction has already left a deep impression on the Third Army.

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: It is no exaggeration when I say that this weapon will completely transform the current stalemate on the northern front.

steps.name: Angry Servant
steps.text: They're acting without the Tsar's permission or the State Council's! They deployed this devastating weapon without even bothering to evacuate the nearby civilians—

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: Nothing grows on that barren soil but weeds. It is the perfect place to test the weapon. Why get worked up over a few vagrants?

steps.name: Angry Servant
steps.text: It is His Imperial Majesty's land, and those were His Imperial Majesty's people!

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Do you have the details?

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: Right here.
The seething servant takes the report and brings it to the Tsar sitting at the end of the hall.
Fyodor flips through the pages in silence, carefully reading through their contents.
The smell of bitter almond fills the empty hall.

steps.name: Angry Servant
steps.text: Your Imperial Majesty...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: (Raises a hand)

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Tell the Marshal that the results are quite satisfactory. However, regarding the requests made in the report—the lost data from Chernobog and further energy supplies...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Grypherburg cannot provide these at this time.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: The priority for Project Zero was to obtain a stable energy supply from the Sarcophagus. This was a hurdle that the Chernobog research never overcame, and our most pressing need.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: But you have chosen to prioritize the weaponization of the Sarcophagus.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: This was not the outcome I wanted when I made Project Zero a national priority.

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: Your Imperial Majesty, the Marshal is ready to fight and triumph over the enemies of Ursus.

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: If you do not support Her High Excellency, you will be allowing the traitors to bash open Grypherburg's gates and plunder the empire's treasures.

steps.name: Angry Servant
steps.text: Insolence! How dare you speak to His Imperial Majesty in such a manner!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yes, Mr. Chairman, Rhodes Island is currently in possession of Dr. Kal'tsit's research and her data on the Sarcophagus...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But we need to ensure Rhodes Island's safety before any agreement.

options: Amiya—

steps.text: You stop mid-sentence as you see Amiya wink at you, realizing that she has an idea.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Yes... it should be a fair trade.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I have devoted many years to making Ursus a more civilized nation, and it is for this vision that I have stood at the Tsar's side all these years. We share the same dream.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I assure you that I will not give up my principles for the sake of convenience, especially not when there is another choice.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I apologize. I meant no offense.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I understand. Caution is a virtue rarely seen in the young.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: But I think we have gone around in circles long enough. What are your terms?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We wish to borrow the Sarcophagus.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: 'Borrow'?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: To what extent? How? And... why?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Here is the plan for your perusal.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: In short, we wish to enter the facility to ascertain the Sarcophagus's unknown function, which Dr. Kal'tsit mentions in her records.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Its what?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We're not certain it truly exists. We are, however, certain that ascertaining it will not damage the Sarcophagus.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit's data indicates that it may be of help to Rhodes Island in our research into the new symptoms of Oripathy, and that the Sarcophagus may be more than just a source of energy.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Policy support from Ursus will, of course, be necessary for any follow-up research.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: So Rhodes Island will share with us this function that may or may not exist.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It's part of Dr. Kal'tsit's research, after all.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: So...

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: All you seek is a solution the existence of which you aren't even sure about.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It may not be important to anyone else, but it's of paramount importance to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: What if the function doesn't exist?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Our agreement still stands.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Even if you get nothing from your investment?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We're prepared.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: What preparations have you made?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What kind of plan do we need to convince the government of Ursus?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: I have retained all of Kal'tsit's data on the Sarcophagus, which will help Ursus restart the Sarcophagus's energy core.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Doctor, you must decide whether we hand the power to restart the Sarcophagus to Ursus again.

options: What do you think, Amiya?
What do you think, Mon3tr?
What do you think, Closure?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If I were the one making the decision, I wouldn't want the Sarcophagus to be controlled by any regime.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But the Ursine Originium mines are drying up, and there are many people who urgently need the Sarcophagus's energy...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: And we need the Sarcophagus's miracle...

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Honestly, I'm not sure.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: We witnessed the tragedy at the lab. No one can guarantee it won't happen again.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: But Kal'tsit decided to seal the Sarcophagus away, rather than destroy it. I think she wanted to believe that there will come a time when the people of Terra will enjoy its benefits.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Oh, you're asking me?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Well... dealing with Ursus is kind of scary. But we have to take certain risks to bring Kal'tsit back.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Maybe I can add another layer of protection for the data. First we use it to reach an agreement with the Ursine government, then we unlock it once we're sure it's the right time.

options: The situation is urgent.
For us, and for Ursus.
We must choose cooperation over conflict wherever we can.
We must all learn to put a little bit of trust in one another.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The data that we are offering will be unlocked in segments in a terminal we provide, fully unlocking once we leave Zelgrad safely.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Any information Rhodes Island obtains from Zelgrad will be shared with you.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: You're not exaggerating when you said you're prepared.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: And it seems you already know the current location of the Sarcophagus.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I expect the location of the Sarcophagus would have been part of any deal we reach.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We simply did some homework.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Yes, you know quite a few things... which saves me the effort of explaining.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: But the information you possess also represents risk factors out of my control. I would not have considered cooperating with you, if our situation was not so dire.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I have one more question for you, my guests.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: This mysterious scholar, known by the mononym Kal'tsit. She came to Ursus from afar, directed research into the Sarcophagus, and sealed it away herself.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: She was neither a subject of Ursus, nor our enemy... and then there is Rhodes Island, who followed in her footsteps, until the two of you sit before me today.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: What exactly are you after?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Would you believe a verbal explanation?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Yes, I want to hear it in your own words.

options: Rhodes Island's answer is not a credible one from the perspective of interests.
We hope you will listen to us from an idealistic perspective.
We hope you'll be willing to believe.
That there are people on this land who are willing to fight for justice, unbound by national borders.
That there are people in this land who want to secure the future for everyone.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Moving words, certainly...
A servant emerges from another door. He approaches the Chairman and bends down.

steps.name: Servant
steps.text: Should I serve wine to our guests?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Bring last year's Taman red wine. The sunlight there was good last year.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: ...I see.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: The name Rhodes Island came to our attention long ago. We have been watching...

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Rhodes Island's deeds have earned you an opportunity for cooperation.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I will write a letter of safe passage to Zelgrad on behalf of His Imperial Majesty. It's the only thing I can do for you right now.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Thank you for your understanding.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: And there's no need to hack the government servers to understand the distance between Grypherburg and Zelgrad.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Zelgrad is Ursus's pride, her 'green city', the 'city of tomorrow'. It objectively welcomes any visitors.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I hope you find what you're looking for there.
Fyodor gazes at the report in his hands, forgetting that he is not supposed to show emotion.
The reporting officer remains utterly calm, unfazed by the Tsar's silence.

steps.name: Polite Servant
steps.text: Would Your Imperial Majesty like some wine?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Mm... what's available?

steps.name: Polite Servant
steps.text: Taman red wine. The grapes there were of good quality last year.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: I will have some, then.

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: Your Majesty.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: I do not say this to criticize Marshal Buterina. The pursuit of strength runs in the veins of every Ursine soldier... and the results have certainly left an impression on the rebels.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Remind Marshal Buterina, however, not to forget the mission the empire has tasked her with—strength is important, but strength alone will neither feed the people nor keep them warm.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: ...I will continue to supply Zelgrad.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: I will also be sending several academicians from the Imperial Institute of Energy Science, in order to assist you with Project Zero's energy research.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: I look forward to similar progress in that area.

steps.name: Angry Servant
steps.text: And why the silence? Are you not pleased by the Tsar's magnanimity?

steps.name: Proud Officer
steps.text: ...The First Army will not disappoint you.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Certainly.

steps.name: Angry Servant
steps.text: Your Imperial Majesty.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: I'm tired, Saveliy. Where is Witte? Still meeting with the guests?

steps.name: Angry Servant
steps.text: His message indicates that a conclusion has been reached. Perhaps the meeting has already ended.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: It's urgent. I must see him, I must...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Ugh—
Fyodor tries to stand, but feels a bout of dizziness and almost falls back upon his chair.
He waves away the servant and presses his own forehead with his hand.

steps.name: Angry Servant
steps.text: It must be that insolent brute!

steps.name: Angry Servant
steps.text: Their marshal brushing off the mistake of forced conscription as merely an 'abundance of caution' was one thing, but how dare a mere captain of the First Army act with such impertinence!

steps.name: Angry Servant
steps.text: How long must we continue to endure, Majesty?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: (Softly) It's not time yet.

steps.name: Angry Servant
steps.text: What was that?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: The scent is dissipating, Saveliy. I can no longer smell the bitter aroma.

steps.name: Angry Servant
steps.text: Ah, I'll refill it—

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Never mind.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Someone was waiting outside the door... the civil representatives from Odoyev Raion, I believe? Have them come in first. And tell them to be at ease.

steps.name: Angry Servant
steps.text: Perhaps you can rest first. There is heat in the corridor; they will not freeze.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: I summoned them. I should not make them wait.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: If I am to know their true thoughts, I must make them trust me, not just fear or worship me.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Ah, there you are.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: How did the meeting go? Not too badly, judging by your faces.
You take out the letter of safe passage.

options: We reached an agreement with the Chairman.
We have an opportunity to approach the Sarcophagus.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I said you'd be fine, but your friends just wouldn't believe me.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hey, you don't get to see an Ursine imperial palace every day.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I guess flying a drone here would be an act of war...

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Looks around warily)

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: I suppose Chairman Witte set conditions in exchange for entry into Zelgrad?

options: We must share some information with them.
They need someone to reveal the secrets of the Sarcophagus.
Chairman Witte bears us no ill will.
Amiya played the part of a consummate diplomat.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, I was nervous!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We got permission, we should set out soon.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Personally, I would love to come with you, but unfortunately, there are other matters that require my attention.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Just one thing... will you have enough hands at the Grypherburg Oripathy treatment center when you're away?

options: Is anyone threatening the safety of the Infected miners?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: You promised they would be safe in Grypherburg.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: They are safe, at least officially... but as I said, things are not so peaceful in the capital right now.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I'll do what I can to protect them, but you should prepare some contingencies.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: I'll be here.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: It would be inconvenient for me to go to Zelgrad with the Doctor. My place is here, protecting Rhodes Island's patients.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I forgot about you. This is much more reassuring.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: One final reminder.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You may have the Council's permission, but don't expect things to go smoothly in Zelgrad.

options: We're used to it.
What's the difference?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I just heard about this, but there has been a change in the First Army garrison at Zelgrad.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: It is now commanded by Anatoliy, Marshal Buterina's only son.

options: Is he dangerous?
Is he difficult?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Ask about Grypherburg in high society, and the most likely answer you'll get is... 'crazy'.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: If half the rumors about him are true, he's not fit to be a soldier, much less a general...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: However, his mother, Marshal Buterina of the First Army, is undoubtedly an intelligent woman.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: She knows Zelgrad's strategic importance. I doubt nepotism is the only reason she made this assignment, at a time like this.

options: We'll be careful.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I hope you find what you're looking for... and help Ursus deal with this headache.

options: Are you calling the Sarcophagus a 'headache'?
Isn't it supposed to be 'hope'?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Headache and hope... why not both?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Well, I shouldn't talk too much about rumors and hearsay.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Stay safe, Doctor.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I don't appreciate being snuck up on from behind.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: ...Sorry.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Mama wants you to babysit me, doesn't she?

spans.text: wants you to babysit me, doesn't she?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: But look at you, a frail and feeble Infected. Ridiculous, isn't it? I might end up having to protect you, should anything happen.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Please don't worry about me, if anything happens.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Of course I won't!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Until then, however, I'll allow you to stay.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: When do we leave?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Never mind that. I have questions. Answer them.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Why is it that I don't feel any more pain, even though the rocks are still there?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: It doesn't hurt anymore... it's strange.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Because all I've done is soothe the pain, to relieve the constant fear of death. People are often confused at first, doubting that it's true...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: How many people have you blessed this way?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Countless.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: So, everyone who seeks your help.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Everyone who suffers.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Did they all see it? That golden, endless river... am I not special?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Why did you show up, claiming that you couldn't cure Oripathy, yet you somehow soothed my pain? What exactly was it that you showed me?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Tell me—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Tell me!
The young man turns around abruptly and grabs Hierda's thin shoulders, as though he thinks he can squeeze the answer out of them.
But Hierda does not understand the reason for his excitement.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Excuse me...?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: The golden, still river! The endless river that I saw when you healed me!

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: You saw—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I only caught a glimpse, but it was when all my pain left me. There must be some meaning to it.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Is that the land of eternity that you talked about? Can everyone go there? But if so...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: What's the difference between this land of eternity and the one beneath our feet?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I'm not sure what you saw, but if it calms and frees you from pain and hatred, perhaps that is your land of eternity.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I'm glad you saw it.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: ...Just seeing it isn't enough.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: How can we go there? Tell me!

steps.name: Distant Voice
steps.text: —Generalik—

steps.name: Distant Voice
steps.text: Did you find him?

steps.name: Distant Voice
steps.text: Blyat, we're supposed to leave ASAP, but neither of them are anywhere to be found—

spans.text: , we're supposed to leave ASAP, but neither of them are anywhere to be found—

steps.name: Distant Voice
steps.text: Did I hear something over there? You, check it out.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Tell me...

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I think someone's looking for us.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: We should go, first. I'll tell you everything you want to know on the way.

steps.name: Attentive Soldier
steps.text: —This is what the apartment's interior looks like. Most of your companions are housed here. It's on the edge of the satellite city, but the facilities are comparable to those in the city center.

steps.name: Attentive Soldier
steps.text: Would you like to go inside?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Of course. Thank you for leading the way...

steps.name: Surprised Vagrant
steps.text: Who's there—

steps.name: Surprised Vagrant
steps.text: Hierda?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Zaya! Is everyone here?

steps.name: Friendly Vagrant
steps.text: Those soldiers herded us into this building. We were all confused, but it turns out it has everything we need, even though it's not much to look at...

steps.name: Friendly Vagrant
steps.text: Don't worry about us!

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: How could I not be worried?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I was wondering where you are, whether you're cold. But it seems that things are much better than I could have imagined.
Hierda turns to the soldier who brought her here.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Please communicate my gratitude to the Marshal.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: For taking care of my companions, and giving them a roof over their heads, to protect them from the wind and snow—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You should thank me.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Of course. Thank you, sir.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You don't know why you should thank me, do you?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I could not have come to visit my companions, if you had not given permission.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Hmph. True enough.
Anatoliy takes a look around, then leans in to Hierda and lowers his voice.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: So they're like me.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Yes. We're all the same. In the end, we'll arrive at the same place in peaceful bliss.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: The 'land of eternity'?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Yes, the land of eternity, as I told you on our way here.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: 'We will all return to the same peace...'

steps.name: Friendly Vagrant
steps.text: Is this gentleman one of us, Hierda?
Hierda looks up into Anatoliy's eyes.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: He—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: ...Hmph.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Of course... he's one of us.

steps.name: Friendly Vagrant
steps.text: When can we leave, Hierda?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Friendly Vagrant
steps.text: We can't stay here forever, can we? This place has everything we need, but there are more Infected out there who need your help.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Of course, we won't stay here forever. For now, however...
Hierda looks up at the gaunt silhouette of the young man in the corridor outside. It is as though the scent of blood in the command room still lingers at the tip of her nose.
She recalls the words that she accidentally overheard on the deck, and clenches her fist as she thinks.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: We're in the custody of the army right now. That Generalik will not let us go easily, and I promised his mother to take care of him during this time.

steps.name: Friendly Vagrant
steps.text: Do you mean—

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: (Whisper) You and Zaya will need to take care of the others, until we're able to leave safely.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: (Whisper) I must keep watch over him... his impulsive nature is a danger, not just to himself, but to others as well.
I think this is the place...
I wrapped Nina in this jacket when the power was out. There must be something wrong with it, that's what made strange things grow from her—
But I had only worn it when washing the clothes of those in white coats—
No, I should have burned it, like burning things contaminated with Originium dust...
But the green spots on it are nothing like Originium dust—

steps.name: Friendly Worker
steps.text: There you are!

steps.name: Friendly Worker
steps.text: There are still two more spots for laundry workers tomorrow. Are you going? I'll put your name in if you are—

steps.name: Friendly Worker
steps.text: Hey, what's up with the outfit? Are you going to work at the Originium factory? But I thought it was closed.
No... I'm not going...
I can't. Nina's still at the clinic.

steps.name: Friendly Worker
steps.text: Oh, I see, alright then. Family comes first.

steps.name: Friendly Worker
steps.text: Say, you haven't gotten sick too, have you? You used to work three jobs every day, wind or rain, but you're letting a well-paying job get away now?
I have to go. Make sure you wash your clothes thoroughly after the job, or—
Or just burn it...

steps.name: Friendly Worker
steps.text: What—

steps.name: Friendly Worker
steps.text: What do you mean? Why should I burn the clothes?

steps.name: Friendly Worker
steps.text: She's been acting weird lately, ever since the number of Infected in the city started rising...

steps.name: Friendly Worker
steps.text: Well, it's not like I have the luxury of worrying about other people.
